close_reason: Done in 7bb173a. Extended ClientConfig::request_timeout field rustdoc to name the DoS-resistance rationale for forbidding Duration::ZERO (reqwest treats ZERO as 'no timeout', not 'instant fail'; positive timeout protects against indefinite hangs / slowloris-style resource leaks). Extended validate() error message to match. No behavior change.
description:
client.rs:129-134 — ClientConfig::validate rejects request_timeout == Duration::ZERO with InvalidArgument

The rejection is correct, but the doc-comment on the field (client.rs:41-43) says "Must be > 0. Use Duration::from_secs(30) for a 30-second timeout."

The contract is sound for the constructor path (JmapClient::new calls config.validate() at client.rs:193). But there is a SECOND failure mode the doc doesn't surface:

reqwest::RequestBuilder::timeout(Duration::ZERO) does NOT mean "fail immediately" — it means "no per-request timeout, only the client-level connect_timeout applies". The reqwest docs are explicit about this. If a future maintainer of this crate accidentally skips validate() (or someone constructs ClientConfig fields directly bypassing the validate call), the resulting JmapClient would have:
  - No request-level timeout (Duration::ZERO is the disable signal in reqwest)
  - Only the 10-second connect timeout from the transport
  - Hangs on any slow server response

The validate() guard is correct defense, but the doc-comment on the field should explain WHY Duration::ZERO is forbidden — otherwise a maintainer looking at it and thinking "why not allow zero as 'disable timeout' since reqwest supports it?" might silently remove the check.

Recommendation: amend the doc-comment at client.rs:41-43 to add: "ZERO is forbidden because reqwest treats Duration::ZERO as 'no timeout' rather than 'instant fail'; this crate enforces an explicit positive timeout to prevent indefinite hangs on stalled servers."
title: ClientConfig request_timeout = 0 silently disables timeout in reqwest, not what validate() docs claim
